questions.q: Two capacitors $C_1$ and $C_2$ are connected in parallel to a battery. Charge-time graph is shown below for the two capacitors. The energy stored with them are $U_1$ and $U_2$, respectively. Which of the given statements is true?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For a capacitor at steady state
$q=C V \text { and } U=\frac{1}{2} C V^2$ Since $C_1$ and $C_2$ are connected in parallel, $V_1=V_2$.
Also from graph $q_1 \lt q_2\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad C_1 V_1 \lt C_2 V_2 \\
& \text { i.e. } C_1 \lt C_2 \text { or } C_2 \gt C_1 \\
& \qquad \frac{U_1}{U_2}=\frac{C_1 V_1^2}{C_2 V_2^2}=\frac{C_1}{C_2} \lt 1
\end{aligned}$
or $U_1 \lt U_2$ or $U_2 \gt U_1$

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor is made of two square plates of side $a,$ separated by a distance $d\left(d ≪ a\right) .$ The lower triangular portion filled with a dielectric of dielectric constant $K,$ as shown in the figure. Capacitance of this capacitor is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Consider a small element at a distance x. It is a two capacitors in series.

$dc = \dfrac{d{c}_{1} \times d{c}_{2}}{d{c}_{1} + d{c}_{2}}$

$dc = \dfrac{{ε}_{0} . adx}{\dfrac{xtan\theta}{k} + \dfrac{d - xtan\theta}{1}}$

$∴ dc = \dfrac{{ε}_{0}K . adx}{- xtan ⁡ \theta\left(K - 1\right) + d . k}$

$∴ C = {∫}_{0}^{a}\dfrac{{ε}_{0}K . adx}{- xtan ⁡ \theta\left(K - 1\right) + d . k}$

$= \dfrac{{ε}_{0}k . a}{tan ⁡ \theta ( K - 1 )}ln\dfrac{- atan ⁡ \theta\left(K - 1\right) + d . k}{d . K}$

$= \dfrac{{ε}_{0}Ka^{2}}{d\left(K - 1\right)}lnK$

questions.q: If the charge on a capacitor is increased by $2C$, the energy stored in it increases by $44 %$. The original charge on the capacitor is (in $C$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy stored in a capacitor is given by& $E = \dfrac{Q2}{2C}$.

Let initial charge be~${Q}_{0}$.

Then,~$1 . 44\left({Q}_{0}^{2}2C\right) = \dfrac{\left({Q}_{0} + 2\right)2}{2C}$

$⇒ 1 . 2{Q}_{0} = {Q}_{0} + 2$

${Q}_{0} = \dfrac{2}{0 . 2} = 10C$

questions.q: Two identical capacitors have same capacitance $C$. One of them is charged to the potential $V$ and other to the potential $2V$. The negative ends of both are connected together. When the positive ends are also joined together, the decrease in energy of the combined system is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The common potential after connection would be, ${V}_{C} = \dfrac{qnet}{Cnet} = \dfrac{CV + C\left(2V\right)}{2C}$

$⇒ {V}_{C} = \dfrac{3V}{2}$

Therefore, loss of energy

$= \dfrac{1}{2}CV^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}C \left(2V\right)2 - $\dfrac{1}{2}$2C \left(\dfrac{3V}{2}\right)$2$

$= $\$left(\dfrac{CV^{2}}{4}\right)$

$

questions.q: Two identical thin metal plates has charge ${q}_{1}$ and ${q}_{2}$ respectively such that ${q}_{1} > {q}_{2}$. The plates were brought close to each other to form a parallel plate capacitor of capacitance $C$. The potential difference between them is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
On bringing the charged metal plates closer, electric field $\overset{→}{E}$ in the intervening space is~$\overset{→}{E} = \overset{→}{E1} + \overset{→}{E2}$

Where

Intensity of field due plate charged by~${q}_{1}$~is~\left|\overset{→}{E1}\right| = \dfrac{\sigma1}{2{ε}_{0}} = \dfrac{q1}{2{ε}_{0}A}$(directed rightwards)

And Intensity of field due to plate charged by~${q}_{2}$~is~

\left|\overset{→}{E2}\right| = \dfrac{\sigma2}{2{ε}_{0}} = \dfrac{q2}{2{ε}_{0}A}$~(directed leftwards)
So, Net field is given by~

$\overset{→}{E} = \overset{→}{E1} + \overset{→}{E2} ⇒ E = {E}_{1} - {E}_{2}$

$∴ E = \dfrac{q1}{2{ε}_{0}A} - \dfrac{q2}{2{ε}_{0}A} = \left({q}_{1} - {q}_{2}\right)2{ε}_{0}A . . . \left(1\right)$

For parallel plate capacitor~$C = $\dfrac{{ε}_{0}A}{d} . . . \left(2\right)$

From above two equations~

$E = \left({q}_{1} - {q}_{2}\right)2Cd . . . \left($3\right)$

$∵$Relation between intensity of field~ \left(E\right)$ and potential difference~ \left(V\right)$ between the plates is~

$E = \dfrac{V}{d} . . . \left(4\right)$

From equation~ \left($3\right)$~and~ \left($4\right)$

$V = \left({q}_{1} - {q}_{2}\right)$2C$

$

questions.q:
The electric field in an electromagnetic wave is given as
$\overset{→}{E} = 20sin\omega\left(t - \dfrac{x}{c}\right)\overset{→}{j}NC^{- 1}$, where $\omega$ and $c$ are angular frequency and velocity of electromagnetic wave respectively. The energy contained in a volume of $5 \times {10}^{- 4}m^{3}$~will be
(Given ${ε}_{0} = 8 . 85 \times {10}^{- 12}C^{2}N^{- 1}m^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that,& $\overset{→}{E} = 20sin\omega\left(t - \dfrac{x}{c}\right)\overset{→}{j}NC^{- 1}$

The average energy density of an electromagnetic wave is~$\dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}E^{2}0$.

The total energy stored is~

${E}_{total } = \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}{E}_{0}^{2} \times volume$

$⇒ {E}_{total} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 8 . 85 \times {10}^{- 12} \times ( 20{)}^{2} \times 5 \times {10}^{- 4} = 8 . 85 \times {10}^{- 13}J$

questions.q:
Two identical parallel plate capacitors, of capacitance $C$ each, have plates of area $A,$ separated by a distance $d$ . The space between the plates of the two capacitors, is filled with three dielectrics, of equal thickness and dielectric constants ${K}_{1}, {K}_{2}$ and ${K}_{3}$ . The first capaciitor is filled as shown in figure $I,$ and the second one is filled as shown in figure $II .$
If these two modified capacitors are charged by the same potential $V$ , the ratio of the energy stored in the two, would be $( {E}_{1}$ refers to capacitor \left(I\right)$ and ${E}_{2}$ to capacitor $( II )$ ):
$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy stored in a capacitor $E = \dfrac{1}{2}CV^{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{{E}_{1}}{{E}_{2}} = \dfrac{{C}_{1}}{{C}_{2}}$

${C}_{1} = {\left(\dfrac{d}{3{ε}_{0}{k}_{1}A} + \dfrac{d}{3{ε}_{0}A{k}_{2}} + \dfrac{d}{3{ε}_{0}A{k}_{3}}\right)}^{- 1}$
$= {\left(\dfrac{d}{3A{ε}_{0}}\right)}^{- 1}{\left(\dfrac{1}{{k}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{k}_{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{k}_{3}}\right)}^{- 1}$
$= {\left(\dfrac{d}{3A{ε}_{0}}\right)}^{- 1}{\left(\dfrac{{k}_{1}{k}_{2} + {k}_{2}{k}_{3} + {k}_{3}{k}_{1}}{{k}_{1}{k}_{2}{k}_{3}}\right)}^{- 1}$

${C}_{1} = \dfrac{3A{ε}_{0}}{d} \left(\dfrac{{k}_{1}{k}_{2}{k}_{3}}{{k}_{1}{k}_{2} + {k}_{2}{k}_{3} + {k}_{3}{k}_{1}}\right)
${C}_{2} = $\dfrac{{ε}_{0}\left(\dfrac{A}{3}\right){k}_{1}}{d} + \dfrac{{ε}_{0}\left(\dfrac{A}{3}\right){k}_{2}}{d} + \dfrac{{ε}_{0}\left(\dfrac{A}{3}\right){k}_{3}}{d}
$∴ \dfrac{{C}_{1}}{{C}_{2}} = \dfrac{{E}_{1}}{{E}_{2}} = \dfrac{9{k}_{1}{k}_{2}{k}_{3}}{\left({k}_{1} + {k}_{2} + {k}_{3}\right)\left({k}_{1}{k}_{2} + {k}_{2}{k}_{3} + {k}_{3}{k}_{1}\right)}

questions.q: A force of $10N$ acts on a charged particle placed between two plates of a charged capacitor. If one plate of capacitor is removed, then the force acting on that particle will be.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Electric field due to each plate,& ${E}_{1} = {E}_{2} = \dfrac{σ}{2{ε}_{0}} = \dfrac{Q}{2A{ε}_{0}}$

Net electric field between the plates,~${E}_{net} = {E}_{1} + {E}_{2} = \dfrac{Q}{A{ε}_{0}}$

Force on charged particle between the plates,~${F}_{1} = q{E}_{net} = \dfrac{qQ}{A{ε}_{0}} = 10N$

Now, in second case, the net electric field,~$E = \dfrac{σ}{2{ε}_{0}} = \dfrac{Q}{2A{ε}_{0}} = 5N$

Force on charged particle,~${F}_{2} = qE = \dfrac{qQ}{2A{ε}_{0}} = 5N$

What are the charges \left(q_1\right.$ and \left.q_2\right)$ on the capacitors $C_1$ and $C_2 when equilibrium condition is reached.
$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{q}_1^{\prime}=6 \times 5=30 \mu \mathrm{C}$ Finally
$\begin{aligned} & 6 \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{C}}+12 \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{c}}=30+0 \\ & 18 \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{C}}=30 \\ & \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{30}{18}=\frac{5}{3} \mathrm{Volt} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{q}_1=\frac{6 \times 5}{3}=10 \mu \mathrm{C} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{q}_2=\frac{12 \times 5}{3}=20 \mu \mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A capacitor $C$ is fully charged with voltage~${V}_{0}$. After disconnecting the voltage source, it is connected in parallel with another uncharged capacitor of capacitance~$\dfrac{C}{2}$. The energy loss in the process after the charge is distributed between the two capacitors is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Heat Loss is given by,&

$H = \dfrac{{C}_{1}{C}_{2}}{2\left({C}_{1} + {C}_{2}\right)}\left({V}_{1} - {V}_{2}\right)2$

${V}_{1}$~is~initial voltage of capacitor~$C= {V}_{0}$

${V}_{2}$~is the initial voltage of capacitor~$\dfrac{C}{2}= 0$

$= \dfrac{c \times \dfrac{c}{2}}{2\left(c + \dfrac{c}{2}\right)}\left({V}_{0} - 0\right)2 = \dfrac{C}{6}{V}_{0}^{2}$

$H = \dfrac{1}{6}{C}_{0}{V}_{0}^{2}$

questions.q: In the network shown below, the charge accumulated in the capacitor in steady state will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In steady state, capacitor behaves as open circuit, so no current will flow.

The total resistance of the circuit is,& $R = \left(6 + 4\right)Ω = 10Ω$

The current flowing through the circuit is

$I = \dfrac{3V}{10Ω}$

Potential difference on~$6Ω$~resistor

$V ' = \dfrac{3}{10} \times 6 = 1 . 8V$

The charge on the capacitor is,

$Q = CV ' = 4\mu F \times 1 . 8V = 7 . 2\mu C$

questions.q: A capacitor has capacitance $5 µ F$~when its parallel plates are separated by air medium of thickness $d$. A slab of material of dielectric constant $1 . 5$ having area equal to that of plates but thickness~$\dfrac{d}{2}$~is~inserted between the plates. Capacitance of the capacitor in the presence of slab will be ______~$µ F$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Capacitance of the parallel plate capacitor when air is present $C = \dfrac{{ϵ}_{0}A}{d} = 5\mu F$

After insertion of dielectric, the equivalent capacitance of the new capacitor is~

${C}_{eq} = \dfrac{{ϵ}_{0}A}{\dfrac{\dfrac{d}{2}}{1 . 5} + \dfrac{\dfrac{d}{2}}{1}}$

$= {ε}_{0}A\left(\dfrac{d}{3} + \dfrac{d}{2}\right) = \dfrac{6{ε}_{0}A}{5d}$

$= \dfrac{6}{5} \times 5\mu F = 6\mu F$.

questions.q: A capacitor ${C}_{1}$ of capacitance $5\muF$ is charged to a potential of $30V$ using a battery. The battery is then removed and the charged capacitor is connected to an uncharged capacitor ${C}_{2}$ of capacitance $10\muF$ as shown in figure. When the switch is closed charge flows between the capacitors. At equilibrium, the charge on the capacitor ${C}_{2}$ is~_____~$\muC$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The initial charge on the& $5\mu F$~capacitor will be~$q = CV = 150\mu C$. If the charge on the~$10\mu F$~capacitor is~$q$~after the key is closed then,

$\dfrac{150 - q}{5} = \dfrac{q}{10} ⇒ q = 100\mu C$

questions.q: In the given figure, the charge stored in $6\muF$ capacitor, when points $A$ and $B$ are joined by a connecting wire is _______\muC.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At steady state, capacitor behaves as an open circuit and current flows in circuit as shown in the diagram.

${R}_{eq} = 9Ω$

$i = \dfrac{9V}{9Ω} = 1A$

$\Delta{V}_{6Ω} = 1 \times 6 = 6V$

${V}_{A} = 3V$

So, potential difference across $6\muF$ is $6V .$

Hence, $Q = C\Delta V$

$= 6 \times 6 \times {10}^{- 6}C$

$= 36\muC$
